neutral_fact_en: [COMPANY_A] hired [COMPANY_B] in 2004 to relocate a gas pipeline on a large tract of wooded, unimproved land. On August 7, 2004, [COMPANY_B] drove a small bulldozer, with its blade raised off the ground, through an area containing grave sites. The plaintiffs alleged that the graves were not indicated on any map, identified in a deed, marked by an obvious sign, included on a government-maintained list, or otherwise reasonably identifiable as an area containing graves. [COMPANY_B] contended that the area was significantly overgrown, contained mostly unmarked grave sites, and had some grave markers buried in forest debris. After the bulldozer operator realized that the bulldozer had passed through the grave-site area, he immediately blocked off the area and relocated the route to connect with the pipeline at a different location. Six plaintiffs claimed that their decedent was buried directly beneath the bulldozer's path, and two others stated that they believed their decedent could be buried beneath that path; however, the plaintiffs' expert was unable to locate a grave shaft directly under the path.
neutral_fact_ko: [COMPANY_A]는 2004년에 숲이 있고 개발되지 않은 넓은 토지에서 가스관을 이전하도록 [COMPANY_B]를 고용했다. 2004년 8월 7일, [COMPANY_B]는 블레이드를 지면에서 들어 올린 상태로 소형 불도저를 묘지가 있는 구역을 통과해 운전했다. 원고들은 해당 묘지들이 어떤 지도에도 표시되어 있지 않았고, 증서에도 명시되어 있지 않았으며, 눈에 띄는 표지로 표시되어 있지 않았고, 정부가 관리하는 목록에도 포함되어 있지 않았으며, 그 밖에도 묘지가 있는 구역으로 합리적으로 식별할 수 없었다고 주장했다. [COMPANY_B]는 해당 구역이 잡초와 초목이 크게 무성했고, 대부분 표시되지 않은 묘지로 이루어져 있었으며, 일부 묘지 표지가 숲의 잔해에 묻혀 있었다고 주장했다. 불도저 운전자는 불도저가 묘지 구역을 통과했다는 것을 깨달은 후 즉시 해당 구역을 차단하고, 다른 위치에서 가스관과 연결되도록 경로를 변경했다. 원고 6명은 각자의 고인이 불도저의 경로 바로 아래에 묻혀 있었다고 주장했고, 다른 2명은 각자의 고인이 그 경로 아래에 묻혀 있을 수 있다고 믿는다고 진술했다. 그러나 원고들의 전문가는 그 경로 바로 아래에서 묘혈을 찾지 못했다.
neutral_fact_source: [COMPANY_A] hired [COMPANY_B] in 2004 to relocate a gas pipeline on a large tract of wooded, unimproved land. On August 7, 2004, [COMPANY_B] drove a small bulldozer, with its blade raised off the ground, through an area containing grave sites. The plaintiffs alleged that the graves were not indicated on any map, identified in a deed, marked by an obvious sign, included on a government-maintained list, or otherwise reasonably identifiable as an area containing graves. [COMPANY_B] contended that the area was significantly overgrown, contained mostly unmarked grave sites, and had some grave markers buried in forest debris. After the bulldozer operator realized that the bulldozer had passed through the grave-site area, he immediately blocked off the area and relocated the route to connect with the pipeline at a different location. Six plaintiffs claimed that their decedent was buried directly beneath the bulldozer's path, and two others stated that they believed their decedent could be buried beneath that path; however, the plaintiffs' expert was unable to locate a grave shaft directly under the path.

source_fact_units.model_source_span: She stepped into a depressed area of the sidewalk, lost her balance, tripped on a raised and uneven area of bricks next to the depression, and fell forward. As a result, she fractured her wrist, necessitating two surgeries. It is undisputed that the raised portion of the sidewalk was less than two inches and that defendant, the city of Lansing, maintained this sidewalk. Plaintiff sued defendant under the highway exception to governmental immunity, alleging that defendant had breached its duty under MCL 691.1402(1) to maintain the sidewalk in reasonable repair. Defendant answered, raising as an affirmative defense the two-inch rule of MCL 691.1402a(2).
